chunks: Ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī narrated through his chain of transmission:
That he was asked about a man who dies and leaves dependents while owing a debt: should they be provided for from his wealth? He said:

If it is certain that what he owes encompasses all of the wealth, then nothing should be spent on them. But if it is not certain, then they should be provided for from the middle measure of the wealth.

key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed by the deceased
key_terms.عِيَالًا: dependents or family members who require maintenance
key_terms.مَالِهِ: his wealth or estate left behind

ai.seo_question: If a man dies in debt, can his family be supported from his estate before the debt is fully assessed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the estate of a deceased person who leaves both dependents and debt. If the debt is known to consume the entire estate, no maintenance is taken from it for the family; if that is not certain, a moderate amount may be spent on them from the estate.
